headline: Circus and carnival permit amendment approved; three letters sent on Rice Street traffic.
summary: Two pothole damage claims, for $275 and $300, were approved, and a $1,349.08 tire claim was denied and referred to J.R. Vinagro Corp. Liquor license renewals were approved, and a letter was sent to Public Works about traffic at the Roosevelt Avenue overpass. Public speakers raised concerns about school zone speed cameras, Flock cameras, and the teacher contract.
decisions: Approved the amendment to Chapter 167 on circus and carnival permits, 3-0.
Approved the consent list of routine licenses, including door-to-door employee permits and tavern renewals.
Approved liquor license renewals in the categories listed at the public hearing.
Approved the hora de cafe at 120 High Street on November 22nd and December 20th, 2026, with food, beer and wine.
Continued the Isla Express liquor license hearing until the first meeting in December.
Approved letting Class B establishments stay open until 3:00 a.m. on January 1st, 2027, with alcohol sales ending at 1:00 a.m.
Approved sending three letters to Public Works and police about Rice Street speeding, signs, and crosswalks.
Approved sending a letter to Public Works about Roosevelt Avenue overpass traffic, a traffic study, and the East Street intersection.
Approved six Rhode Island Energy pole petitions, pending approval by the Public Works director.
Approved the appointment of Michael William Cooper to the Juvenile Hearing Board, 6-0.
Denied the $1,349.08 tire damage claim and referred it to J.R. Vinagro Corp., 6-0.
Approved $275 for Napoleon Gonzales and $300 for Nicholas Jensen, both for pothole damage, 6-0.
discussion: Circus and carnival rule: Members discussed naming the charity in the application up front, and a 25% donation the clerk's office had suggested that the ordinance does not state.
Rice Street speeding: Residents described speeding cars, two rollover crashes, and a dog killed on Rice Street, and asked for speed bumps, a one-way street, or solar stop signs.
School zone speed cameras: A speaker asked for an independent audit of the program, saying the $50 tickets and tax refund offsets hurt families.
Flock cameras: Speakers asked the city to remove the cameras, citing privacy, data retention, and misuse, and to spend the money on other safety options.
Teacher contract vote: A teacher asked for a Finance Committee meeting so the Pawtucket School Committee contract could go to a full council vote.
